claim: Open small LLMs (3B, three unrelated families) keep an actual value and an alternative value side by side for a non-actual space (painting, belief, dream, past, hypothetical); both stay linearly decodable after intervening text (base 0.96, alternative 0.94, chance 0.25).
agent_test: Compare a prompt with explicit labelled spaces against an unlabelled hypothesis list on a multi-hypothesis tracking task at equal tokens.

claim: Binding a value to a scope is done by low-dimensional binding-ID or space-index vectors; swapping them swaps what the model believes (Feng & Steinhardt: >99% control, <3% after one swap, >97% after double swap). Steele et al. extend this to space types (transfer index 0.71-0.89; Qwen 0.73 with CI [0.67,0.78] straddling the 0.7 bar). Different tasks, so related but not one confirmed mechanism.
agent_test: Tag every claim with its space name in written state and measure cross-space leaks versus untagged state.

claim: Binding is retrieval-shaped, not a persistent slot: in 3B models a distractor entity's colours decode at the target token almost as well as the target's (advantage +0.07 Qwen, +0.09 Pythia), falling to about 0 within about 16 filler sentences.
agent_test: Interleave two hypothesis spaces with filler; compare restating state per space before each query versus once at the top.

claim: Reporting a value and using it in a rule are causally separate in 3B models (colour subspace flips report 1.00 but rule result 0.00; consequent subspace flips rule 1.00, report 0.32; principal cosine 0.11/0.17). A model can state what a space holds yet not apply it. Pythia could not do the rule task.
agent_test: Ask for stated contents and for a derived consequence separately; add a consistency check when they disagree and measure error rate at equal tokens.

claim: Frontier models (gpt-4o, Qwen-72B, Gemini-2.5, GPT-4.1, Claude, Llama-70B) hold up to eight coexisting stated bindings with no swap errors; derived inference under load is the harder part (Llama-8B 0.31). Scoped-space scaffolds likely add little for plain stated bindings in strong models and more for derivation.
agent_test: Scoped-space state versus flat notes on stated-binding items versus derived-inference items at equal tokens.

claim: Hand-built steering directions (diff-of-means) do no better than random for controlling space value (0.583 vs 0.583); learned low-rank subspaces do (DAS rank-1 0.883 in one seed, 0.96 mean over 3 seeds; rank-4 1.000).
agent_test: Not applicable to a prompt scaffold; relevant only if activation steering is ever used.

claim: Filtering a story to what one character knows before answering raises false-belief accuracy a lot (SimToM): GPT-4 ToMI false belief 25.5 (0-shot) / 74.25 (CoT) / 87.75; GPT-3.5 67.25 / 34.0 / 81.0; BigToM false belief GPT-3.5 41.0 / 56.25 / 70.5. Verified in the paper tables.
agent_test: Two-call filter-then-answer versus single-call CoT at matched total tokens on a multi-agent-knowledge task.

claim: SimToM's gain needs the two-step separation: merging steps into one prompt drops GPT-3.5 ToMI FB 81.0 to 58.75; replacing perspective filtering with generic reasoning gives 31.75. Oracle human perspective gives 96.
agent_test: Ablate: filter and answer in one call versus two calls at the same total tokens.

claim: Explicit symbolic belief graphs per character (SymbolicToM, depth 2), with only the relevant sub-graph given to the model, give very large gains and survive paraphrase: GPT-3 davinci +38 to 92% average; Flan-T5-XL +62 first-order FB; GPT-3.5 +78 second-order FB; LLaMA-7B D1/D2/D3 99/92/88; supervised models collapse on paraphrase (TTT -54, finetuned GPT-3 about -40).
agent_test: Per-agent belief list in the state, answer only from the matching list, versus a single shared state.

claim: Two different methods (prompt-level perspective filter, code-built belief graph) both show that scoped context beats shared context on belief tasks, in the same direction. This supports the principle, not any specific number. Third method (thought-tracing, 2025): GPT-4o ToMi 59.5 plain, 67.0 CoT, 76.0 with weighted per-agent hypotheses.
agent_test: Run both styles on the same item set; check gain by belief order.

claim: Standard false-belief success is brittle: trivial alterations (transparent container, relabelled container) flip GPT-3.5 answers; adversarial sets drop models sharply (e.g. transparent access 66.7 to 0 on some models). Reported ToM gains partly reflect pattern matching. Contrary view: Kosinski reports GPT-4 solves 75% of 40 tasks. Gap search: current reasoning models pass most altered tasks but still score 0 on transparent-container and relationship-change variants (Claude, Grok-3-mini, R1; GPT-5-high 0.5 on one), two items per cell.
agent_test: Evaluate any space-scoping gain on perturbed variants, not only the canonical item.

claim: Models pass single belief questions but fail consistency across question types about the same fact: FANToM short context, GPT-4 0613+CoT All 26.6 (All* 18.4) versus human 87.5; the October GPT-4 version is lower (All 14.8); CoT trades inclusion errors for exclusion errors.
agent_test: Add a cross-question consistency check (who knows what, who could answer) before answering; measure joint accuracy.

claim: Nested spaces get harder with depth: Hi-ToM accuracy falls from near perfect at order 0 to near zero at order 4 for most models (GPT-4 32k overall 60.42 standard, 64.04 with CoT); main error cause is skipping steps and answering a lower order. Steele et al. report no bleed for shallow nested spaces at ceiling, so depth matters. Gap search 2026: for 2025-2026 models the fall is real but not to zero. HiToM order 0 to 4: GPT-o3 0.996 to 0.467, DeepSeek-R1 0.988 to 0.196, DeepSeek-V3 0.979 to 0.608. Second-order ToM costs 10-20 points in Hanabi. An explicit written stack was not tested.
agent_test: Explicit written stack of nested spaces versus unstructured CoT on order 3-4 items at equal tokens.

claim: Backward belief inference (infer the agent's earlier percept from their action) is much worse than forward: GPT-4 0-shot forward belief .97, forward action .79, backward belief .40. A second group (Zhu et al.) finds backward belief Both 0.40 for Mistral-7B even with steering that lifts forward belief to 0.97. In thought-tracing, removing the perception-inference step costs 7 to 20 points. No prompt-level hypothesis-first test on 2025-2026 models for the backward case.
agent_test: Check whether opening a space for 'what did they perceive' first helps backward items at equal tokens.

claim: LMs only weakly switch to a counterfactual space: preference for the counterfactual-consistent ending after an 'if' premise is near chance for several models, and most barely change when 'In reality' follows (they follow lexical triggers). Only 9.4-50% of small-set items are right in both conditions (chance 25). Models tested are old (GPT-2/3, BERT family).
agent_test: Explicit 'In supposition X: ...' framing versus bare 'if', with 'in reality' follow-ups, on a current model.

claim: Counterfactual worlds with changed rules cost accuracy across 11 tasks even when the model passes a check that it understands the counterfactual (GPT-4 two-digit addition: base 10 100.0, base 9 23.4, base 11 38.4, base 8 82.3, base 16 63.0; 0-shot CoT only 38.6 / 56.5 for bases 9 / 11). Gap smaller for more common counterfactuals (recitation). Table values verified.
agent_test: Restate the rule set of the hypothetical space before each step versus not, at equal tokens.

claim: Human readers set up counterfactual and false-belief contexts quickly and use them predictively (eye-tracking, ERP), while real-world knowledge still has some effect. Supports separate spaces with some leakage in humans. Sample sizes and effect sizes not read. Added detail: truth-value N400 effects in counterfactuals match real-world sentences (Nieuwland & Martin 2012, abstract), yet counterfactual mood still adds 0.72 microvolt N400 to world-true words (Kulakova & Nieuwland 2016, N=30, F(1,22)=8.44), and switching back from a counterfactual to the factual world shows early interference then recovery (N=48).
agent_test: None directly; behavioural basis only.

claim: Frame-shifting and blending have processing costs in humans (larger N400 for metaphoric and mapping endings; frame-shifting jokes read slower), but amplitudes and timings were not recorded and the work comes from the theory's own lab. Coulson & Van Petten 2002 used N=18, N400 300-500 ms; no amplitudes extracted.
agent_test: Not testable on the agent; background only.

claim: Entity-state tracking across operations works mainly in models with code in pretraining; accuracy falls with the number of operations and finetuned T5 generalises poorly. Earlier headline results were inflated by trivial cases (62.7% of Alchemy beaker states equal the initial state; probe 86.8% on trivial, 3.1% on non-trivial). Verified.
agent_test: Written state table updated after each operation versus recomputing from the story; vary operations up to 12.

claim: Belief tracking in LLMs uses an entity-binding circuit plus a visibility lookback, and belief status is linearly decodable and steerable in mid-layer heads (>80% probe accuracy, Mistral-7B). Mechanistic evidence that scoped belief representations exist inside models.
agent_test: None at prompt level; supports plausibility of S2 only.

claim: Out-of-scope content leaks into reasoning: one irrelevant sentence leaves under 30% of base problems solved consistently (GSM-IC); regenerating the context to keep relevant parts lifts LLaMA-2-70B factual QA 62.8 to 80.3 (S2A) and GSM-IC in-topic 51.7 to 61.3.
agent_test: Filter-then-answer versus single pass on distractor-laden context; count the filter call in the token budget.

claim: Models accept coherent context over memory, but evidence order swings results by over 5 points (over 30 for PaLM2 and Llama2-7B), so order effects among hypothesis spaces are expected.
agent_test: Shuffle the order of hypothesis spaces in the state; measure variance.

claim: Holding several abstract hypotheses as separate candidates and testing each (Hypothesis Search) lifts an ARC 100-problem subset: direct 17%, abstract hypothesis generation 23%, LLM-summarised 30%, human-selected 33%. Verified. Not a mental-spaces test as such.
agent_test: Scoped-hypothesis scaffold versus best-of-N at equal tokens on ARC items; ARC portfolio is the honest control.

claim: No direct test of Fauconnier-style mental spaces as a prompting method was found. The nearest are SimToM, SymbolicToM and the Steele et al. mechanistic paper (a single-group July 2026 arXiv preprint, models of 3B and under for mechanism).
agent_test: Run our own: scoped space state versus flat state on multi-hypothesis tasks at equal tokens.

claim: Belief is not specially separated from other space types: belief-to-modal/hypothetical transfer exceeds the ordinary between-class baseline by only +0.03 to +0.09; 14B readout transfer is asymmetric (counterfactual 0.33/0.86). Contested against formal-semantics views that treat belief as special.
agent_test: One uniform space-tag format for all space types versus type-specific formats.

claim: The founding theory and its AI parallels (Fauconnier, Fauconnier & Turner, Dinsmore partitions, Sapper, sarcasm and humour analyses) are descriptive, lack experimental numbers and come mostly from proponents. They give design vocabulary, not effect evidence.
agent_test: None.

claim: Scoped, weighted per-agent hypotheses (thought-tracing, 2025) beat flat CoT on ToM benchmarks and match or beat native reasoning models at lower token cost: GPT-4o ParaphrasedToMi 59.5 plain, 67.0 CoT, 76.0 TT; MMToM-QA GPT-4o+TT+CoT 69.0 vs o3-mini-medium 69.0 with under half the tokens (authors' statement). Gains were uneven: Qwen2.5-72B got no FANToM gain from TT alone, and TT+CoT hurt GPT-4o and Gemini on true-belief ToMi items. Only ToM; no flat-hypothesis-list control at equal tokens.
agent_test: Run a multi-hypothesis task with scoped hypothesis blocks versus a flat hypothesis list, same token budget, report per-condition accuracy.

claim: More reasoning does not fix scoped belief tracking in 2025-2026 models: reasoning models do not consistently beat non-reasoning ones on HiToM (o3 0.747, DeepSeek-V3 0.694, R1 0.549, Qwen3-8B-Reasoning 0.481 vs Qwen3-8B 0.558). Removing answer options, stopping early, or capping tokens helps (R1 0.549 to 0.691 without options; Qwen3-8B-Reasoning 0.706 at a 1,500-token cap). Reasoning models also over-assume false belief (o1 true-belief 36-49%).
agent_test: Cap deliberation steps in scoped states and include true-belief and shared-knowledge control items so over-separation shows up.

claim: For current models, classic false-belief scoping is near ceiling and robust to prompt changes (reasoning models), yet scene-visibility alterations still fail (transparent container, relationship change score 0 for Claude thinking, Grok-3-mini, R1). Authors read the gain as more reliable convergence, not new ToM; samples are tiny (two items per cell).
agent_test: Add an explicit visibility check ('what could X see or know from where X was') inside each scope; test on altered-scene items.

claim: Humans show small, localised leakage between worlds: no delay in mapping words to a counterfactual world when the context constrains (Nieuwland & Martin 2012), a 0.72 microvolt N400 cost for world-true words in counterfactual antecedents (N=30), and early interference when switching back from counterfactual to factual (N=48, early window not significant, later recovery). The cost sits at entering and leaving a space.
agent_test: Make open and close of each space explicit steps; on close, restate the base state before using it.

claim: No measured gain from conceptual blending as a prompting method was found. A 2026 paper on blending in humans and LLMs is a conceptual analysis with a toy script; the two 2025 LLM blending works it cites were not located. Human blending carries an N400 cost (N=18).
schema_part: none (blends are in SCHEMA section 4b not to add)
agent_test: Do not add a blend operator unless a measured gain appears.

claim: Unrevised early content leaks forward in long interactions: LLMs lose 39% on average from single-turn to multi-turn over six tasks (200,000+ simulated conversations), mostly through unreliability, because models lock in early assumptions and do not recover. This is indirect evidence for leakage; no study varied the number of scoped spaces or context length with space-binding as the outcome.
agent_test: Reset or restate scoped state each turn; measure cross-scope errors against number of spaces.
